chunks: And with this chain, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The prayer of the two Eids is two rak'ahs; there is no [prayer] before them and no [prayer] after them.

key_terms.الْعِيدَيْنِ: The two Eids (Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Ghadir/Eid al-Adha depending on context)

ai.seo_question: How many rak'ahs are in the Eid prayer and are there prayers before or after it?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal* establishes the concise legal structure of Eid prayers as two rak'ahs without attached Sunnah prayers, reflecting the Shafi'i and Hanbali view often cited in Shia jurisprudence. It highlights the distinct ritual simplicity of Eid compared to daily prayers, emphasizing the communal nature of the occasion as noted in the chapter's introductory context.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 6. And from the previous chain from al-Hussain b. Sa’eed from Fadhalah from Ibn Sinan from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “
Salaat of Eid-ul-fitr and Eid- e-Qurban consists of two rakats and there is no Salaat before and after it.”
